meaning: The only failures `node scripts/pdf-audit/run.mjs --strict` accepts. Each names one probe, one assertion kind (scripts/pdf-audit/gate.mjs KINDS) and a pattern of the failure text; status `deliberate` = bm-render follows CSS or its own API on purpose (a row of docs/PDF_AUDIT.md says so), `open` = a known difference not resolved yet. Another probe, another kind, another failure text, or an exception no failure matches (stale) fails the strict gate. `golden`: the differences scripts/pdf-compare.mjs --strict accepts, per fixture and part (content, an interchange part, fonts); status `noise` = float noise within or just past the comparison bound, explained per fixture.

exceptions.match: ^huge: error: bm "invalid page size" vs takumi "\(renders\)"$
exceptions.reason: bm-render rejects a 1e9 x 1e9 px page (no PDF viewer can open a page past 14,400 user units); takumi writes it. docs/PDF_AUDIT.md, JS API surface: size.

exceptions.match: ^json source: text: bm \["Node text Tailwind"\] vs takumi \["\[object Object\]"\]$
exceptions.reason: `{ json }` input is a bm-render extension that renders the node tree; takumi stringifies the object and prints `[object Object]`. docs/PDF_AUDIT.md, JS API surface: input.

exceptions.match: ^bad json: error: bm "invalid node JSON" vs takumi "\(renders\)"$
exceptions.reason: The same `{ json }` extension validates its JSON and rejects a malformed tree; takumi renders the stringified object. docs/PDF_AUDIT.md, JS API surface: input.

exceptions.match: ^page 1 differs\. Content stream at token 50 .*operator sequence identical\)$
exceptions.reason: takumi ignores the gradient interpolation colour space (`in oklch`) and interpolates in sRGB; bm-render interpolates in the space CSS asks for, so the shading samples differ while the operators are the same. docs/PDF_AUDIT.md, Not ported: gradients interpolated in sRGB.

exceptions.match: ^page 1 differs\. Content stream at token 50 .*operator sequence identical\)$
exceptions.reason: takumi ignores the gradient interpolation colour space (`in oklab`) and interpolates in sRGB; bm-render follows CSS Color 4. docs/PDF_AUDIT.md, Not ported: gradients interpolated in sRGB.

exceptions.match: ^page 1 differs\. Content stream at token 50 .*operator sequence identical\)$
exceptions.reason: takumi ignores `in hsl longer hue` and interpolates in sRGB; bm-render interpolates hue the long way round as CSS asks. docs/PDF_AUDIT.md, Not ported: gradients interpolated in sRGB.

exceptions.match: ^page 1 differs\. Content stream at token 50 .*operator sequence identical\)$
exceptions.reason: takumi ignores `in srgb-linear` and interpolates in sRGB; bm-render interpolates in linear light as CSS asks. docs/PDF_AUDIT.md, Not ported: gradients interpolated in sRGB.

exceptions.match: ^page 1 differs\. Content stream at token 0 \(33 vs 0 tokens; operator sequence DIFFERENT\)$
exceptions.reason: A box-shadow without a colour uses currentColor in CSS; takumi draws no shadow at all, bm-render draws it in the current colour. docs/PDF_AUDIT.md, Painting: box-shadow.

exceptions.match: ^page 1 differs\. Content stream at token 1 .*operator sequence DIFFERENT\)$
exceptions.reason: takumi's parser rejects `inset() round a / b` (elliptical corner radii) and drops the clip; bm-render clips as CSS Shapes defines. docs/PDF_AUDIT.md, Painting: clip-path.

exceptions.match: ^page 1 differs\. Content stream at token 1 .*operator sequence DIFFERENT\)$
exceptions.reason: takumi's parser rejects this `ellipse()` form and drops the clip; bm-render clips as CSS Shapes defines. docs/PDF_AUDIT.md, Painting: clip-path.

exceptions.match: ^page 1 differs\. Content stream at token 1 .*operator sequence DIFFERENT\)$
exceptions.reason: takumi rejects `ellipse()` without radii (closest-side defaults) and drops the clip; bm-render clips as CSS Shapes defines. docs/PDF_AUDIT.md, Painting: clip-path.

exceptions.match: ^page 1 differs\. Content stream at token 1 .*operator sequence DIFFERENT\)$
exceptions.reason: takumi does not parse a basic shape followed by a geometry box and drops the clip; bm-render uses the reference box CSS names. docs/PDF_AUDIT.md, Painting: clip-path.

exceptions.match: ^page 1 differs\. Content stream at token 9 .*operator sequence DIFFERENT\)$
exceptions.reason: takumi drops `clip-path: margin-box`; bm-render writes one clip equal to the border box (no margin here), so the painted result is the same with one extra clip operator. docs/PDF_AUDIT.md, Painting: clip-path.

exceptions.match: ^page 1 differs\. Content stream at token 1 .*operator sequence DIFFERENT\)$
exceptions.reason: takumi does not parse a lone geometry box (`content-box`) and drops the clip; bm-render clips to the content box as CSS Masking defines. docs/PDF_AUDIT.md, Painting: clip-path.

exceptions.match: ^page 1 differs\. Content stream at token 48 .*operator sequence DIFFERENT\)$
exceptions.reason: takumi drops `clip-path: border-box` on a rounded box; bm-render clips to the rounded border box as CSS Masking defines. docs/PDF_AUDIT.md, Painting: clip-path.

exceptions.match: ^page 1 differs\. Content stream at token 109 .*operator sequence identical\)$
exceptions.reason: takumi does not support `mask-mode` and always uses alpha; bm-render applies the luminance mask CSS asks for. docs/PDF_AUDIT.md, Painting: mask-mode / mask-clip / mask-origin.

exceptions.match: ^page 1 differs\. Content stream at token 30 .*operator sequence DIFFERENT\)$
exceptions.reason: takumi does not support `mask-clip`; bm-render clips the mask to the content box as CSS asks. docs/PDF_AUDIT.md, Painting: mask-mode / mask-clip / mask-origin.

exceptions.match: ^page 1 differs\. Content stream at token 16 .*operator sequence identical\)$
exceptions.reason: takumi does not support `mask-origin`; bm-render positions the mask from the content box as CSS asks. docs/PDF_AUDIT.md, Painting: mask-mode / mask-clip / mask-origin.

exceptions.match: ^page 1 differs\. Content stream at token 8 .*operator sequence identical\)$
exceptions.reason: `position: sticky` creates a positioned box in CSS (paints in the positioned layer); takumi paints it as static. docs/PDF_AUDIT.md, Painting: position sticky.

exceptions.match: ^page 1 differs\. Content stream at token 1 .*operator sequence DIFFERENT\)$
exceptions.reason: takumi's parser rejects keyword positions in `circle(... at <keywords>)` and drops the clip; bm-render clips as CSS Shapes defines. docs/PDF_AUDIT.md, Painting: clip-path.

exceptions.match: ^page 1 differs\. Content stream at token 1 .*operator sequence DIFFERENT\)$
exceptions.reason: takumi's parser rejects `circle(... at top left)` and drops the clip; bm-render clips as CSS Shapes defines. docs/PDF_AUDIT.md, Painting: clip-path.

exceptions.match: ^cssVariables option, full document: page count: bm 5 \| takumi 3
exceptions.reason: bm-render applies the `cssVariables` option to `@page` of a whole HTML document too (`@page { margin: var(--m) }` gets 40px, so more pages); takumi leaves the variable unset there. docs/PDF_AUDIT.md, Page model: cssVariables reaching the page context.

exceptions.match: ^cssVariables option, full document: text per page: bm
exceptions.reason: The same cssVariables difference: with the 40px @page margin the lines land on other pages, so the text per page differs. docs/PDF_AUDIT.md, Page model: cssVariables reaching the page context.

takumi turns a `content: url()` image of a pseudo-element into a block, so each part gets its own P; bm-render keeps it inline as CSS does, so one P holds the four leaves. docs/PDF_AUDIT.md, Painting: content url().
The parent tree follows the same single P of the inline generated image (see the structure-tree exception of this probe). docs/PDF_AUDIT.md, Painting: content url().

exceptions.match: ^definite height: what follows comes after the last table fragment \(Chrome\): word positions differ: page 4: bm \["After",7\.5,52\.9\] vs takumi \["After",7\.5,7\.9\]$
exceptions.reason: A table of a definite height with a repeated thead whose last row is cut in the free space of its cells: Chrome (Playwright Chromium printed to PDF, checked 2026-11-23) lays the last table fragment out below the repeated thead (the rest of the row, the spacing) and the block after the table follows it; takumi places that block at the top of the last page, over the repeated thead. bm-render follows Chrome. docs/PDF_AUDIT.md, Page model: table border spacing and rowspans at a break.

takumi has no vertical writing modes and lays the text out horizontally; bm-render lays it out vertically (CSS Writing Modes 4), so the text is drawn through a turned transform, upright glyphs as outlines under an invisible copy of the line. docs/PDF_AUDIT.md, Not ported: vertical writing modes.
